title: When the Wolf Sings Revisited
premise: Ada Ishikawa poisons herself nightly so the crown can eat safely, but her true work is keeping the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things, which trades in favors, names, and doors between realms. When a dying courier presses a map of the broken covenant into her hands, Ada discovers she is the last living signatory's heir — and the usurper's armies will burn the free cities unless someone reforges the pact between human and wolf-kind. Guided by a disgraced guildsman and a wolf-singer who has forgotten her own song, Ada must choose between her sworn duty to the crown and the found family that claims her. In the end, Ada sings the covenant anew at terrible personal cost, binding herself to both realms, and the free cities hold — not through armies, but through a taster who finally belongs.
about_author: C. M. Vane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval trade ledgers before turning to fantasy. They write about people whose quiet, meticulous work becomes the hinge on which kingdoms turn.

chapters.title: The Taster's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. We meet Ada mid-ritual: tasting the queen's supper, recording the poison's progress in her own body, then slipping to the guildhall to balance impossible accounts. A dying courier collapses at her door with a map and a name — hers. Emotional beat: the loneliness of duty cracked open by sudden, unwanted inheritance.

chapters.title: Doors Between Realms
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Ada and Sera, the wolf-singer. The map leads them through a guild-door into the borderlands, where they gather allies: Bramble, a disgraced guildsman; Kesh, a runaway apprentice. They learn the covenant broke when the last signatory fled — Ada's grandmother. Emotional beat: wary strangers becoming a makeshift family around a campfire.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Price
chapters.summary: Sera's POV dominates. The usurper's inquisitors capture Kesh and offer a trade: the map for the boy. Ada refuses to sacrifice him, exposing the group to ambush; Sera's forgotten song stirs when Ada bleeds on the covenant stone. Emotional beat: love against duty — Ada betrays her crown oath to save her chosen family.

chapters.title: When the Wolf Sings
chapters.summary: Full ensemble POV. At the ruined covenant circle, with the usurper's vanguard hours away, Ada claims her inheritance as signatory. The price: her voice and her immunity, traded into the pact itself. Sera remembers the song; together they reforge it. The armies falter at the border as old oaths wake. Emotional beat: belonging won not by blood or duty, but by choice — and its cost borne gladly.
